newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche sees 96/97 profit steady, sales up.
newsitem.headline: Porsche sees 96/97 profit steady, sales up.

text.p: German sports car manufacturer Porsche AG on Tuesday forecast that its profit in the current 1996/1997 year to July 31 would match the level reached in 1995/1996.

Porsche said in a statement the introduction of its Boxster two-seat cabriolet next year -- its first new car in nearly two decades -- would push vehicle sales up to 30,000 units in 1996/97 from around 20,000 in 1995/96.
Porsche said it would be able to keep earnings steady in 1996/97 because it was continuing to raise efficiency in all areas and because fixed costs and labour costs would rise only modestly.

Porsche issued the statement ahead of a news conference to outline 1995/1996 results, which were released earlier this month and showed a surge in net profit to 48 million marks ($30.7 million) from 2.1 million marks.
That enabled the company to pay its first preferred dividend since 1991/1992, 2.50 marks.
